messages:
maria: heads up — multiple customers reporting failures when ingesting embeddings from /v1/embeddings. responses are returning dim=1536 but our indexer schema currently expects 768. first reports ~10:02 UTC, errors are 400 with 'vector_dim_mismatch'.

ingest-bot: alert triggered: indexer-rejects > 50 in 5m for workspace: acme-corp, error_code: VECTOR_DIM_MISMATCH, sample_id: 7d9c1f

daniel: ack, looking. any config changes rolled in last 6 hours?

maria: not on our side — we rolled quantization profiles yesterday but that should only affect model packaging for dedicated. however a CI job bumped the default model variant for /embeddings to gpt-embed-xl (1536) in the hosted catalog at 09:40 UTC.

lee: that lines up. indexer schema migration to 768 was applied last week (migration id 2026-04-09-vec-schema). so older indexers are still on 768 and hosts are now returning 1536 vectors.

sara: customer impact = failures to index + increased latency (retries). some tenants auto-retry, causing peak ingestion spikes. reported P1 from support queue.

julian: can someone paste the exact error payload from the indexer? need to show to product for rollback decision.

daniel: paste below — sample from indexer logs:
```
ERROR [ingest-worker] 2026-03-15T10:04:12Z indexer.go:412 "vector_dim_mismatch" {"expected":768, "got":1536, "doc_id":"acme-12345"}
```

maria: repro steps for support team:
1) curl POST to /v1/embeddings with sample text
2) observe response: {"data":[{"embedding":[0.001, ... total 1536 numbers ...]}]}
3) attempt to call our indexer ingestion API -> 400, vector_dim_mismatch

sara: customer reported example payload attached in ticket #TI-4821. We should provide an immediate mitigation while we triage root cause.

lee: mitigation options:
- short term: rollback catalog change to the 768-sized variant (if available) OR route affected customers to a compatibility shim that downsamples/embeds to 768 (not ideal).
- medium: run backfill on indexers that require 1536 and migrate schema + storage (heavy).
- quickest: mark hosted model variant as opt-in and switch default back to 768 model (config change).

maria: I can flip the hosted default to the 768 variant now if ops approves. will that stop new failures immediately?

daniel: yes for new requests. existing queued embedding batches that already got 1536 will still fail until the index accepts 1536 or we re-ingest.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-451 — "embed-dim-mismatch-hosted-default". Slack incident channel created: #incident-INC-2026-451.

maria: executing rollback now: updating catalog.default_variant -> gpt-embed-base-768. command:
```
# admin-cli set-catalog-default --model gpt-embed-base-768 --env hosted
```

maria: done. config change propagated to staging and primary region at 10:12 UTC.

daniel: monitoring for new rejects... ingest rejects dropped to near-zero after 10:15 UTC. good.

sara: customers seeing fresh successful ingests now — letting them know.

julian: next steps for durable fix:
- product to decide whether hosted default should remain 768 or we should roll indexers to support 1536.
- infra to produce a targeted migration plan for index shard format if we choose 1536.
- support to coordinate backfills for impacted customers that accepted 1536 vectors between 09:40–10:12 UTC.

lee: rough backfill plan (for support/infrastructure):
- identify affected docs by query: indexing.rejected where error=VECTOR_DIM_MISMATCH AND ts between 2026-03-15T09:40:00Z and 2026-03-15T10:12:00Z.
- for each affected tenant, spawn backfill job with rate-limits: 200 docs/min to avoid hotspotting indexer.
- backfill command example:
```
# using ingest-cli
ingest-cli backfill --tenant acme-corp --from-ts 2026-03-15T09:40:00Z --to-ts 2026-03-15T10:12:00Z --batch-size 64 --concurrency 4
```

maria: addendum — before running backfill we must ensure the indexer is in the matching schema (either migrated to 1536 or still 768 and accepting 1536 via compat path). currently we rolled hosted back to 768 so backfill should re-emit embeddings using the 768 variant.

daniel: I ran a dry-run for acme-corp; backfill estimate: 12k docs -> ~1hr at 200 docs/min.

sara: assigned owners: maria -> hosted rollback + customer comms; lee -> indexer migration plan if product chooses 1536; julian -> product decision owner; daniel -> run and monitor backfills.

ops-bot: assigned on-call: @daniel for INC-2026-451.

maria: support reply drafted to customers: "We rolled a change that briefly made the embeddings default 1536. We've reverted the default and are re-ingesting failed documents for affected tenants. We expect most backfills to complete within 1–2 hours. If you see any residual failed items please escalate to support."

julian: long-term notes: we should add a safety gate in the catalog deploy flow: require explicit opt-in when changing embedding vector size for hosted default; add a canary window that only affects 5% of tenants for 1 hour.

lee: logging/observability improvements: add metric embedding_output_dim per-hosted-request and indexer.accepted_dim with alerts when mismatch rate > 0.1% over 5m.

sara: support will close ticket after backfill confirmation and postmortem. please paste final incident timeline in #postmortems.

maria: backfill kicked off for acme-corp at 10:30 UTC. monitoring dashboards show steady throughput, rejections gone.

daniel: done — playlists: backfill jobs running: acme-corp (job 7123), beta-inc (job 7124), gamma-llc (job 7125). ETA per job in job UI.

maria: will update INC-2026-451 with final numbers once all jobs complete. thanks all for quick triage. :thumbsup:

sara: closing loop with customers now.

ops-bot: incident INC-2026-451 status -> monitoring, started 2026-03-15T10:05:00Z, mitigation applied 2026-03-15T10:12:00Z, backfills started 2026-03-15T10:30:00Z."
